edits.find: - **A rule id is a closed union, and closing the last side of it is the live area:** [#449](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/449) is open in review on [#452](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/pull/452).
edits.replace: - **A rule owns its severity and its payload, and closing that is the live area:** [#449](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/449) is open in review on [#456](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/pull/456), which supersedes slice 4 of [#452](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/pull/452) and depends on its slice 1.

edits.find: `ids` is discriminated by which rules own one, and the five producers that build a diagnostic from a rule id they hold as data take that payload as an argument list derived from the rule, so a diagnostic carrying ids its rule never names fails `typecheck` at the call site that built it and one omitting ids its rule always names fails with it. It is not merged, and the runs that measured it belong to that pull request.
edits.replace: `contract/rule.ts` owns what each rule is, checked total against that enumeration by `satisfies`, and `Diagnostic` is flat again: `severity` derives from the rule and `ids` is required and empty for a rule that names none, so `asDiagnostic`, `DiagnosticFields` and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` are deleted rather than re-justified. One constructor builds every diagnostic and the five producers forward to it; four raw literals in `graph/` and the constructor's own `severity` parameter, which thirteen sites still pass, are what remain owed. Green on `0931c0a` at all seven jobs; it is not merged, and the runs that measured it belong to that pull request.
